target_note: Target was 4-8h; run took 54 minutes. Bounded by three things, none of them running out of work: the census was parallelised across five readers (310 rows, 63 findings, 761k tokens of reading in twelve minutes of wall clock); every route the prompt asks for is blocked on a table that cannot be applied because the prompt correctly forbids database access; and the fallback queue was worked to 10 of 12 items rather than the required 8. The next step needs either a database or a decision from Andri.

schema.deviation: rate_books was requested and deliberately not added. agreements.rate_references already is the rate book; what it lacks is UNIQUE (cost_factor_id, code, effective_from). CREATE UNIQUE INDEX can fail on existing duplicates and this migration is otherwise unfailable, so the dedupe-then-index sequence is specified as a separate migration with its duplicate query supplied. It needs a database, which this prompt does not authorise.
schema.rollback: One transaction: drop 11 tables in reverse dependency order, then 11 types. Nothing outside the slice references any of it. Stays true only until the first route lands.

very_tldr: Core billing was a complete, tested, unreachable calculation library - 10 of its 11 modules had zero production callers because there was nothing to write to. Built the 11 tables under it (generated, unapplied), a pure mapper that refuses seven contradictions rather than guessing, and a tenant-scoping guard wired into npm run check. A 310-row source census refuted six written claims and turned up three launch blockers nobody was looking for, one of which is live today: every driver sees a figure 100x too large.
